title: What the live paper record shows
description: The engines' own state, read from the running record: what is open, what closed, and what the market filter is doing right now.
body:
What the live paper record shows. Paper signals only. No real orders are placed anywhere in this record. A single trade says nothing about a strategy. The record below is the engines' own state: what is open, what closed, and what the market filter is doing right now. Live starts: engine 005 counts its live record from 1 October 2026 and engine 006 from 9 October 2026. The live signal was an ATOM entry at 2.066 after the 10 October 2026 daily close. ATOM exited below its 10-day low at the 18 October 2026 close, at 1.703, which is -17.9% after the 30 bps round trip. A NEAR entry at 5.896 on 12 October 2026 has been open since. In testing, losses were more common than wins and the average winner was roughly +19%, so a losing start is the expected case rather than a surprise. The same numbers appear on the performance page, in the signal log, and in the status posted to the channel.

## Open positions

- htf-rsi-007 has 0 positions open on paper.
- trend-daily-005 has 0 positions open on paper.
- trend-daily-006 has 0 positions open on paper.
- A NEAR entry at 5.896 on 12 October 2026 has been open since.

With no open positions on the named engines, the paper record is currently between signals. That means the most recent closed trades define the whole live history for each engine. The open NEAR position is the exception named in the record; it remains open because its exit condition has not triggered. This is a description of state, not a statement about expected outcome. Because every position here is paper, these states describe simulated orders rather than real exposure.

## Closed trades

- htf-rsi-007 closed trades so far: 4, average null net per trade.
- trend-daily-005 closed trades so far: 6, average -13.22% net per trade.
- trend-daily-006 closed trades so far: 7, average -13.34% net per trade.
- ATOM exited below its 10-day low at the 18 October 2026 close, at 1.703, which is -17.9% after the 30 bps round trip.

The closed-trade averages are negative for both trend-daily engines and null for htf-rsi-007. Those are measurements of what happened, not explanations of why a future trade will behave the same way. The ATOM trade is the concrete example behind the live signal: entry at 2.066 after the 10 October 2026 daily close, exit below the 10-day low at 1.703 on 18 October 2026, net -17.9% after 30 bps round trip. A single trade cannot validate or invalidate either engine. The record reports null for htf-rsi-007, so no average net per trade should be read into that figure.

## Market filter

- trend-daily-005: the Bitcoin market filter is off.
- trend-daily-006: the Bitcoin market filter is off.
- trend-daily-005 closest to its 20-day breakout: TRXUSDT is 9.82% below its high.
- trend-daily-005 closest to its 20-day breakout: BNBUSDT is 10.43% below its high.
- trend-daily-005 closest to its 20-day breakout: UNIUSDT is 12.53% below its high.
- trend-daily-006 closest to its 20-day breakout: TRXUSDT is 9.82% below its high.
- trend-daily-006 closest to its 20-day breakout: BNBUSDT is 10.43% below its high.
- trend-daily-006 closest to its 20-day breakout: UNIUSDT is 12.53% below its high.

When the Bitcoin market filter is off, the trend-daily engines are not allowing new entries under that rule. The listed distances to 20-day breakout highs show how far the nearest candidates are from triggering a breakout entry under the same measurement. Those distances are current readings, not forecasts of whether or when a breakout will occur. The same names appear for both engines because the record lists them for both.

## Record and updates

- The same numbers appear on the performance page, in the signal log, and in the status posted to the channel.

The record updates continuously, so the counts, averages, and distances above are a snapshot rather than a final verdict. Because every position here is paper, the figures describe simulated entries and exits rather than real orders. The snapshot above was read at 2026-11-11T14:56:21.519Z; later reads may differ. The same numbers appear on the performance page, in the signal log, and in the status posted to the channel. Nothing in this record should be treated as proof that any rule will produce the same result again.
